## Overview

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| **Input** | DESeq2-style contrast table: `Gene`, `Comparison`, `log2FoldChange`, `padj`, optional `stat` |
| **Key packages** | `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `readr`, `stringr`, `tibble`, `igraph`, `ggplot2`, `scales` |
| **Statistics** | Hand-rolled signed-regulon TF activity score (`sum(mor × de_score) / sqrt(scored targets)`, direction from the sign of the raw score); prior-network overlap; causal sign propagation from the perturbation node |
| **Output** | TF volcano/heatmap, TF-to-prior-network diagnostics, recurrent-edge overview, module-specific causal networks, Cytoscape-ready exports (`.csv`, `.sif`, `.dot`) |
| **Download** | [template.Rmd](template.Rmd) |

::: {.callout-important}
**This is a demo, not a production TF-activity pipeline.** The regulon table, the prior
knowledge network and the "recurrent CARNIVAL edges" are all small `tribble()`s written
inline in `template.Rmd`. The template does **not** call `decoupleR`, `OmnipathR` or
`CARNIVAL`, and it does not download anything — that is what keeps it reproducible offline.
Its purpose is to demonstrate the *shape* of the workflow and to give you working plotting,
sign-propagation and Cytoscape-export code to hang a real analysis on.

To do the real thing, swap `toy_collectri()` for a `decoupleR` regulon (e.g. CollecTRI via
`OmnipathR`), replace the inline `pkn` tribble with a real signed prior network, and replace
the cached `carnival_edges` with actual `CARNIVAL` solver output. Those packages are not in
`install_packages.R` precisely because this template never calls them.
:::

Edit the `## ── USER CONFIGURATION` block at the top of `template.Rmd`. Point `DEG_FILE`
at your own DESeq2 contrast table to run the demo statistics over real data; the networks
will still be the bundled toy ones until you replace them.
